cards.name: Waypoint graph path search
cards.summary: A star search across area waypoints that each carry their own height above the floor plane
cards.behavior: Loading turns each area waypoint into a search vertex built from its planar coordinates plus a height read from a per-point table; points missing from that table are placed on the zero plane instead of being rejected. A query snaps the start and the goal to their nearest vertices by squared distance and answers with a straight two-point segment whenever the vertex set is empty or both endpoints snap to the same vertex. The frontier repeatedly takes the open vertex with the lowest accumulated distance plus a straight-line estimate to the goal, moves it to the closed set, and stops as soon as the goal vertex is taken, then walks the parent links back into an ordered path. Neighbours already closed are skipped, and a neighbour already open is replaced only when the new accumulated distance is lower. If the open set drains without reaching the goal, the search still returns a straight segment so callers always get a route.

constants.name: missingVertexHeight
constants.unit: world units on the vertical axis, substituted once per waypoint when the graph loads

capabilities: nearest-vertex snapping for both endpoints
open-set replacement only when the new distance improves
straight-segment fallback for empty graphs and unreachable goals

cards.name: Creature path following
cards.summary: Waypoint stepping with an arrival radius, a path reuse window and a shortcut to the final destination
cards.behavior: A movement request is refused outright while the creature's movement is restricted, which is how a combat exchange keeps an attacker in place. Otherwise the planar squared distance to the goal is compared with the square of the requested arrival radius, and reaching it drops the stored path and returns the movement type to idle. An existing path is reused when its destination matches the new goal or when it was found no more than one second earlier; any other case asks the area for a fresh route. While following, the final destination replaces the next waypoint whenever the destination is nearer than that waypoint, and once the squared distance to the current target falls to one the waypoint index advances instead of moving. The actual step is delegated to the area, and the walk or run animation is selected from whether that step succeeded.

constants.name: pathReuseWindow
constants.unit: milliseconds of wall-clock time, compared once per creature update

constants.name: waypointAdvanceDistanceSquared
constants.unit: squared world units, compared once per creature update

capabilities: arrival radius compared in squared space
path reuse keyed by destination or age
waypoint skipping toward the final destination
movement refusal while movement is restricted

cards.name: Walkmesh stepping and wall sliding
cards.summary: Per-step sweep over walkmeshes with normal-projected sliding, a downward ground snap and a room update
cards.behavior: One step first turns the creature to face the requested direction, lifts the origin slightly above the floor, multiplies the creature's walk or run speed by the frame delta and sweeps that distance along the requested direction while excluding any walkmesh owned by the mover. A blocking hit does not end the step: the direction is projected onto the horizontal perpendicular of the hit surface normal and swept a second time, so a creature slides along a wall instead of stopping dead, and only a second blocked sweep gives up. Ground height is then resolved by casting a long ray downward onto walkable surfaces and keeping the nearest walkable hit, which also supplies the new room, the surface material and the vertical position written back to the creature. A room change notifies the party leader hook so room visibility and the camera target refresh, and the step finishes by testing area triggers at the new position.

constants.name: stepOriginLift
constants.unit: world units on the vertical axis, applied once per movement step

constants.name: elevationProbeDrop
constants.unit: world units of downward probe reach, one probe per movement step

constants.name: walkProbeLength
constants.unit: world units of horizontal sweep reach, up to two sweeps per movement step

capabilities: slide along wall normals instead of stopping
vertical snap from a downward walkmesh probe
mover excluded from its own collision sweep
walkable surface filter by material

cards.name: Action queue execution
cards.summary: Per-object action list that runs one action per frame and gates interactions on arrival distance
cards.behavior: Every object owns a queue of actions. Each update first drops completed actions from the front of the queue, then promotes delayed actions whose timers have elapsed, then executes only the new front action with the frame delta, so a long queue advances at one action per frame rather than all at once. Interaction actions re-test arrival on every update and therefore share a single approach distance: opening a door, closing it, searching a container and using the security skill all walk to within two units before acting, while a plain move-to-point order completes at a one unit radius. The attack action only registers a combat round once the target is inside the attacker's attack range. Clearing the queue from outside also returns the creature to the idle movement type.

constants.name: objectInteractionDistance
constants.unit: world units, re-tested once per action update

constants.name: moveToPointArrivalRadius
constants.unit: world units, re-tested once per action update

capabilities: one action advance per object update
timer-based promotion of delayed actions
shared arrival distance across interaction actions

cards.name: Camera-relative leader movement
cards.summary: Held direction keys resolved against the camera yaw, with a walk modifier and action cancellation
cards.behavior: Direct control only applies to the party leader and is skipped entirely while the leader's movement is restricted. Held direction keys resolve to an angle offset from the third-person camera yaw: forward follows the camera, back adds a half turn, and the two strafe directions add and subtract a quarter turn, after which the angle is converted into a planar unit direction with the horizontal component negated. Any movement request clears the leader's queued actions and asks the area to step the leader in run mode unless the walk modifier is held, so keyboard movement takes priority over queued orders. When no direction is held and the queue is empty, the leader returns to the idle movement type. Walk and run speeds come from the appearance table and fall back to one world unit per second when the table has no entry.

constants.name: walkSpeedFallback
constants.unit: world units per second, applied with the frame delta

constants.name: runSpeedFallback
constants.unit: world units per second, applied with the frame delta

capabilities: camera-relative direction with quarter-turn strafing
walk modifier overriding run
direct input cancels queued actions

cards.name: Third-person orbit camera
cards.summary: Accelerating yaw orbit, relative mouse look, style-driven offsets and line-of-sight pull-in
cards.behavior: Held rotation keys drive the orbit yaw: rotation speed starts at the minimum, grows with accumulated frame time up to the maximum, integrates into yaw and wraps at a full turn. Holding the right mouse button switches to relative mouse look, where each pixel of horizontal motion subtracts a small fixed yaw step and the camera transform is rebuilt immediately. Placement pads the target point along the view direction, offsets the eye by the style distance along that direction, raises it by the style height, and then trims the target-to-eye segment to the first walkmesh hit so level geometry never sits between camera and leader. The target itself comes from the leader model's dedicated camera hook when present, otherwise from the model bounds centre. The default style supplies a three point two unit distance, a zero point four five unit height and a fifty-five degree vertical field of view; the style also carries a pitch value that this revision never applies. Entering combat swaps the orbit to a second style slot, although in this revision the combat lookup writes its table entry into the default slot, so the combat slot is never filled from the table.

constants.name: orbitMinSpeed
constants.unit: radians per second, integrated with the frame delta

constants.name: orbitMaxSpeed
constants.unit: radians per second, integrated with the frame delta

constants.name: orbitAcceleration
constants.unit: radians per second squared, integrated with the frame delta

constants.name: mouseLookRadiansPerPixel
constants.unit: radians per pixel of horizontal mouse motion, applied per motion event

constants.name: targetPadding
constants.unit: world units along the view direction, recomputed per camera update

constants.name: defaultStyleDistance
constants.unit: world units behind the target, recomputed per camera update

constants.name: defaultStyleHeight
constants.unit: world units on the vertical axis above the target, recomputed per camera update

constants.name: defaultStyleViewAngle
constants.unit: degrees of vertical field of view, fixed when the camera loads

capabilities: yaw acceleration ramp with wrap
relative mouse look while the right button is held
camera pull-in on level geometry
style-driven distance, height and field of view

cards.name: Conversation camera framing
cards.summary: Speaker and listener shot variants built from the gap between bodies, with occlusion pull-in
cards.behavior: Conversation framing derives a direction and a gap from the listener to the speaker and centres the shot on the midpoint between them, then positions eye and target for each variant. Close-up variants offset the eye from the midpoint by a quarter of the gap both along and across the view direction, each offset capped at one unit, lift it a tenth of a unit and shift the aim point a tenth of the gap to one side of the subject. Far variants sit half the gap to the side of the speaker or listener position and aim at the midpoint. The two-subject variant pushes the eye two and a quarter times the gap to the side, capped at four units, lifts it a quarter unit and aims a quarter unit below the midpoint. After placement the target-to-eye segment is trimmed to the first walkmesh hit, and the final transform inverts a look-at from eye to target with a world up axis.

constants.name: closeUpOffsetFraction
constants.unit: fraction of the speaker-to-listener gap, recomputed per framing change

constants.name: closeUpOffsetCap
constants.unit: world units, recomputed per framing change

constants.name: closeUpLift
constants.unit: world units on the vertical axis, recomputed per framing change

constants.name: farOffsetFraction
constants.unit: fraction of the speaker-to-listener gap, recomputed per framing change

constants.name: bothSubjectsOffsetFraction
constants.unit: fraction of the speaker-to-listener gap, recomputed per framing change

constants.name: bothSubjectsOffsetCap
constants.unit: world units, recomputed per framing change

constants.name: bothSubjectsAimDrop
constants.unit: world units on the vertical axis below the midpoint, recomputed per framing change

capabilities: per-variant shot composition from the body gap
gap-relative offsets with distance caps
occlusion pull-in before the shot is committed

cards.name: Combat round timing
cards.summary: Three second rounds split at the half mark, with duel appends and a post-round combat tail
cards.behavior: Registering an attack starts a round keyed by the attacker. An attack against someone already mid-round is folded in as the second attack of that round only when the roles are reversed and the round has not yet passed half its duration, which marks the exchange as a duel and gives both sides one resolution in the same round. Round time advances with the frame delta and clamps at the round duration. The first attack's result applies at the half mark, where the projectile is removed, an off-hand attack may resolve, and a queued second attack starts; the second result applies at the round duration. Ranged attacks launch their projectile a short delay after each half begins. Finishing a round completes the queued action, clears the attack target and the movement restriction, schedules combat deactivation eight seconds later and runs the end-round script.

constants.name: roundDuration
constants.unit: seconds, advanced by the frame delta

constants.name: projectileDelay
constants.unit: seconds after each half-round mark, advanced by the frame delta

constants.name: combatDeactivateDelay
constants.unit: seconds, counted down by the frame delta

constants.name: duelAppendWindowFraction
constants.unit: fraction of the round duration, compared once per attack registration

capabilities: half-round resolution split for two attackers
duel append window before the half mark
delayed combat deactivation after the round
one round per attacker with per-update time clamp

cards.name: Attack roll and critical threat
cards.summary: Single d20 against defense with automatic hit, automatic miss and a confirming threat roll
cards.behavior: Defense comes from the target creature when the target is a creature, and falls back to a flat ten for doors, placeables and other objects. The attack rolls one twenty-sided die: twenty always hits, one always misses, and every other result hits only when the roll plus the attacker's attack bonus reaches defense. A successful attack then checks the weapon's critical threat window: when the roll exceeds twenty minus the weapon's threat value, a second die plus the main-hand attack bonus is compared against defense to upgrade the hit into a critical. Unarmed attacks carry a threat of one, so a critical needs a roll of twenty and still has to confirm.

constants.name: rollMinimum
constants.unit: die face, one roll per attack

constants.name: rollMaximum
constants.unit: die face, one roll per attack

constants.name: nonCreatureDefense
constants.unit: defense points, compared once per attack

constants.name: unarmedCriticalThreat
constants.unit: threat points, one comparison per successful attack

capabilities: automatic hit on twenty and automatic miss on one
flat defense for non-creature targets
weapon threat window with a confirming roll

cards.name: Defense and attack bonus from abilities
cards.summary: Defense as ten plus the Dexterity modifier, and attack bonus from class table, ability and hand usage
cards.behavior: Defense is ten plus the Dexterity modifier, and the modifier halves the difference between the ability score and ten using integer division, so a score of eight yields a penalty of one while a score of nine truncates to zero. An ability score that was never assigned defaults to eight. Attack bonus aggregates the class attack-bonus table over all class levels, then adds the Strength modifier for melee attacks or the Dexterity modifier for ranged attacks, and subtracts the handedness penalties when a weapon occupies the off hand. The same ability modifier is added to both ends of the damage range reported for the equipped weapon, so a high Strength shifts the whole spread rather than only its maximum.

constants.name: baseDefense
constants.unit: defense points, recomputed per defense query

constants.name: abilityBaseline
constants.unit: ability points, applied once per modifier query

constants.name: abilityDivisor
constants.unit: integer divisor, applied once per modifier query

constants.name: defaultAbilityScore
constants.unit: ability points, fixed when no score was assigned

capabilities: truncated ability modifier around a ten point baseline
melee uses Strength while ranged uses Dexterity
class table attack bonus summed across levels

cards.name: Damage dice and multiplier
cards.summary: Weapon dice rolled per hit, floored at one and scaled by the critical multiplier
cards.behavior: A weapon contributes a dice pool built from its die count and die size, and every die is rolled between one and its size; an unarmed strike reports a flat one point. The rolled total is floored at one so an attack always registers, then multiplied by the critical multiplier, which is two by default and otherwise comes from the weapon. Hits that arrive with a pre-computed amount skip the dice entirely and apply that amount, and critical hits with a pre-computed amount multiply it. Damage is applied as an instant effect that subtracts from current hit points with a floor of zero, raised to one when the target is flagged to keep at least one hit point.

constants.name: minimumRolledDamage
constants.unit: hit points, floored once per damage roll

constants.name: defaultCriticalMultiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on rolled damage, applied once per critical hit

constants.name: dieMinimumFace
constants.unit: die face, one draw per die

constants.name: unarmedBaseDamage
constants.unit: hit points, fixed per unarmed strike

capabilities: dice pool sized by the equipped weapon
damage floor so every hit registers
critical multiplier applied after the floor
hit point floor with a keep-alive target flag

cards.name: Two-weapon penalties and off-hand strike
cards.summary: Fixed handedness penalties plus a second resolution from the off-hand weapon each round
cards.behavior: When both weapon slots are filled, the attack bonus takes a fixed penalty of six points on the main hand and ten points on the off hand before the level and ability contributions are added. Any weapon in the left slot marks the creature as two-weapon fighting, which makes every successful half-round resolution follow up with a second attack roll against the off-hand weapon and its own critical threat window, using the off-hand penalty and the off-hand critical multiplier. The off-hand strike resolves immediately after the main attack in the same update, so both land inside one round. Dueling and two-weapon feats are not modelled in this revision, so the penalties never shrink, and extra attacks from feats or force powers are not added.

constants.name: mainHandPenalty
constants.unit: attack points deducted, fixed while both hands hold a weapon

constants.name: offHandPenalty
constants.unit: attack points deducted, fixed while both hands hold a weapon

capabilities: asymmetric main-hand and off-hand penalties
second attack roll in the same half round
off-hand critical threat and multiplier

cards.name: Projectile launch and flight
cards.summary: Ranged rounds spawn a projectile at a weapon hook and advance it toward a target attachment
cards.behavior: A ranged round resolves the attacker's right-hand weapon and the ammunition type it fires, takes the weapon attachment's bullet hook as the launch point when that node exists, and aims at the target model's impact attachment, falling back to the model origins when either node is absent. The resulting direction is normalized, and the projectile model is attached to the scene root after signalling a detonate event by name. Each update moves the projectile along that fixed direction at sixteen world units per second and yaws it to face its travel direction, derived from the arc tangent of the direction components. The projectile is removed just before the attack result is applied at the half-round mark, so travel time never gates whether the hit lands.

constants.name: projectileSpeed
constants.unit: world units per second, integrated with the frame delta

constants.name: projectileLaunchDelay
constants.unit: seconds after the half-round mark, advanced by the frame delta

capabilities: launch point from a weapon attachment node
aim point from a target attachment node
constant-speed travel with facing from the direction
projectile removed before damage resolves

cards.name: Sight and hearing sweeps
cards.summary: One second perception sweep with a hearing radius, a sight radius, a facing cone and an occlusion probe
cards.behavior: A timer runs the perception sweep once per second. For every living creature the sweep measures the planar squared distance to each other creature and compares it against the squared hearing and sight ranges taken from the range table: hearing is pure distance, while sight additionally requires the planar direction to the target to fall within sixty degrees of the creature's facing and a clear segment between two eye points, each raised above the object position. Entering and leaving each set fires a first-heard, inaudible, first-seen or vanished notification that scripts can react to, so each transition fires once rather than every sweep. Hostility used for combat orders and cursor feedback is a separate lookup that compares a faction reputation value against a neutral midpoint.

constants.name: perceptionInterval
constants.unit: seconds between sweeps, counted down with the frame delta

constants.name: eyeHeight
constants.unit: world units added to both ends of the sight probe, one probe per candidate per sweep

constants.name: sightHalfAngle
constants.unit: degrees from facing in the ground plane, one comparison per candidate per sweep

capabilities: separate hearing and sight ranges per creature
planar facing cone combined with an occlusion probe
transition-only notifications instead of per-sweep polling

cards.name: Party roster and follow steering
cards.summary: Leader-first roster with leader rotation and script-issued follow actions that steer behind the leader
cards.behavior: The roster keeps at most three members and always holds the leader first, refusing a fourth member. Asking for a different leader by identity reorders the list so that member becomes first, while the quick rotate control swaps positions, using separate two-member and three-member orderings, then clears every member's queued actions and re-runs the leader-moved hook so room visibility and the camera target follow the new leader. Following is never automatic: a script routine queues a follow-leader action, and each update that action reads the leader position and steers toward a five unit follow distance, switching to run once the squared planar distance to the leader exceeds the walk threshold, which puts the effective run range near two units. A separate follow-object action steers toward an arbitrary object with a script-supplied distance and compares squared distance against the squared walk threshold.

constants.name: maxPartyMembers
constants.unit: members, fixed roster limit

constants.name: followDistance
constants.unit: world units from the leader, re-evaluated once per action update

constants.name: walkThreshold
constants.unit: squared world units on the ground plane, compared once per action update

capabilities: leader-first roster capped at three members
leader rotation clearing member action queues
follow steering with a run threshold and follow distance

cards.name: Door state and module transition
cards.summary: Door click routing, walkmesh swaps on open and close, and the module change a linked door schedules
cards.behavior: Clicking a door routes to a transition handler: a door linked to another module schedules a module change using the door's linked module name and entry tag and returns without opening anything, while an unlinked door that is still closed queues an open action for the party leader. A door carries three walkmeshes taken from its model, one closed variant and two open variants; opening plays the opening animation, enables the first open variant and disables the closed mesh and the second open variant, and closing plays the closing animation and reverses those toggles. The open action approaches to the shared interaction distance of two units, and a locked door runs its fail-to-open script instead of opening unless the actor is the door itself. Door placement keeps the vertical axis upright and uses only the stored bearing as a yaw rotation.

constants.name: doorUprightTilt
constants.unit: radians on the two horizontal axes, applied once when a door loads its transform

constants.name: objectInteractionDistance
constants.unit: world units, re-tested once per action update

capabilities: linked door schedules a module change instead of opening
closed and open walkmesh variants toggled with the animation
locked door defers to a fail-to-open script
yaw-only door placement on an upright axis
